chapter_title: Concerning the Dragon with Fourteen Heads; what it

6.original: [and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by]
6.content: and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by

spiritual_reading:
No monstrous power exists as a bodily thing in the way the unillumined imagine. What was spoken was given from a state of untouched reception of influx, and it was not understood by those who stayed in external knowing; yet the utterance was directed to spiritual realities.

The teaching is about the natural degree as it is when it is taken for the whole of life, and so is counted as a ruling falsity made persuasive by the senses. This ruling falsity is the doctrine of life from the self-sense; and the many powers by which it governs are the following.

First are the complete set of outward receptions through which the natural mind takes in and judges appearances: the twofold power that admits visual impressions, the twofold power that admits auditory impressions, the twofold power that admits olfactory impressions, and the discriminating reception that sorts and chooses according to relish, taking in innumerable variations as they present themselves.

These are the full set of chief outward inlets in the higher part of the natural. Beneath them are the corresponding inward-acting powers in the lower part that execute and confirm what the higher inlets suggest: a twofold power of drawing in and expelling as to the life of the natural, a twofold power of moving and acting as to its strength, and a central governing power that presides over the whole lower domain and so supports the ruling activity of the higher inlets. Together, the higher inlets and the lower executors make a complete sufficiency of dominant agencies by which the doctrine of the self rules in both what is received and what is done.

In the opposite description, the hidden seats and interior gatherings in which that ruling falsity is harbored and from which it thrusts itself outward are these: the delight of sensuous discrimination that claims authority to decide good and true by what pleases; the general breathing of the natural mind that sustains its continual motion of thought; the central love of the natural that gives heat to its intentions; the obscure support that hoards and hardens what is unclean and unexamined; and the common life circulating through these interiors, by which their quality is carried into every function. When it looks outward from those interiors and displays itself in both the higher receptions and the lower executors, it fights by all its dominant agencies.

Whoever recognizes these workings as one with the bodily-minded thought that would rule, and resists it, and prevails until its dominion in him is ended, comes forth into freedom without the harm that otherwise attends that conflict when the outer life is put off.

This, then, is the instruction: that the ruling falsity of life from the self is present with a complete sufficiency of governing agencies and with interior seats where it hides; and through these it continually drives its craving to rule.

fills.notes: The substrate contrast is between a virginal receptivity (unmixed, unappropriated influx) and the Magi’s externalizing literalism. “State of purity” keeps the impersonal cosmological register while matching the spiritual sense: “untouched reception of influx.”

fills.fill: because they remained in outward knowing
fills.notes: The spiritual translation requires the reason for non-understanding: fixation in externals. This is stated as a condition of cognition, not a moral rebuke, consistent with the oldest layer.
The surviving letters “spiri” constrain this strongly; the sense demands that the written words are about spiritual realities, not a corporeal monster.
The sentence needs a verb of comparison: the earth, taken in the natural sense, “is likened to it” (to a dragon) as a correspondential lesson.

fills.fill: and a great deceit is joined
fills.notes: The spiritual context: the natural degree taken as the whole is “counted” a persuasive ruling falsity. “Deceit joined” conveys the persuasive falsity attached to the natural appearance.
Introduces the didactic turn (“I will instruct you about this”), matching the impersonal expository style without adding Mani’s dialogic framing.
The dragon is identified as “this doctrine”; the spiritual sense specifies it is a doctrine of life from the self-sense, not a mere opinion.
Completes “of the flesh” in the substrate register: “flesh” corresponds to proprium, self-derived life. This keeps the impersonal cosmological causality.
The list of seven upper ‘heads’ ends with the tongue; specifying its placement (“in the mouth”) fits the natural description while preserving the correspondence (sensuous discrimination).
Transitions from the seven above to the seven below: an enumerative connective is demanded by structure (“These are…; and the seven… below”).
Matches the spiritual sense: “twofold power of drawing in and expelling as to the life of the natural,” corresponding naturally to inhalation and exhalation.
Matches the second lower pair in the spiritual sense: “moving and acting as to its strength,” corresponding naturally to locomotion and manual action.
Introduces the “central governing power” (the ruler) as midmost/presiding, consistent with the correspondential structure: a single governor over the lower domain.

fills.fill: and reveal its likeness and its observation above and below, it wages war by
fills.notes: Kept as given. It expresses the correspondential mechanism: from interior ‘dens’ it looks out, manifests in higher and lower functions, and then combats by the full set of agencies (fourteen heads).

fills.fill: and uproots it from his members.
fills.notes: The required outcome is not merely killing a creature but ending dominion within the embodied faculties. “Uproots… from his members” matches the spiritual sense: “until its dominion in him is ended,” in an impersonal, structural idiom.
The spiritual translation ends with “craving to rule.” Restoring “desire to rule” fits the visible fragment “des” and keeps the oldest-layer cosmological focus on dominion rather than moral passion.

assessment: Most gaps are structurally constrained by the correspondential mapping already present: seven upper inlets, seven lower executors, five interior seats, then outward manifestation and combat. Exact physiological naming for the ‘seven of the torso’ is less tight in the surviving natural text, so those restorations are moderate and expressed in functional (correspondential) terms rather than later institutional or devotional language.
